title: ANALISIS OPINI NETIZEN PADA KOMENTAR INSTAGRAM TERKAIT BANJIR SUMATERA 2025 (Studi pada Akun Instagram Narasi Newsroom, Kompas, Detik, dan CNN Indonesia)
abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui topik, sentimen, dan emosi yang muncul dalam komentar netizen pada unggahan Instagram media pemberitaan terkait penanganan banjir Sumatera 2025. Latar belakang penelitian ini didasarkan pada meningkatnya diskursus publik mengenai respons pemerintah dalam situasi krisis bencana, khususnya setelah munculnya polemik terkait tidak ditetapkannya banjir Sumatera 2025 sebagai bencana nasional. Instagram dipilih sebagai objek kajian karena kolom komentar pada platform ini menjadi ruang publik digital tempat masyarakat menyampaikan kritik, dukungan, solidaritas, serta evaluasi terhadap kebijakan pemerintah. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif deskriptif berbasis Computational Text Analysis (CTA). Data penelitian berupa 59.256 komentar Instagram yang dikumpulkan dari unggahan akun media pemberitaan terkait banjir Sumatera 2025 pada periode 27 November hingga 3 Desember 2025. Teknik analisis data dilakukan melalui tahapan preprocessing, word cloud, topic modelling menggunakan BERTopic, sentiment analysis, dan emotion analysis. Fokus analisis diarahkan untuk melihat bagaimana publik mengevaluasi respons pemerintah melalui pola percakapan, kecenderungan sentimen, dan ekspresi emosional yang berkembang di ruang digital. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa percakapan publik tidak hanya berfokus pada kondisi bencana, tetapi juga berkembang menjadi ruang evaluasi terhadap respons pemerintah. Hasil topic modelling memperlihatkan dominasi topik yang berkaitan dengan kritik, tuntutan pertanggungjawaban pejabat pemerintah, distribusi bantuan, kondisi daerah terdampak, isu kerusakan lingkungan, serta persepsi pencitraan pemerintah selama krisis. Sentimen negatif menjadi kecenderungan dominan dalam komentar publik, yang mencerminkan ketidakpuasan, kritik, dan rendahnya kepercayaan masyarakat terhadap penanganan krisis. Sementara itu, hasil emotion analysis menunjukkan bahwa respons publik tidak hanya bersifat rasional dan politis, tetapi juga dipengaruhi oleh emosi kolektif seperti kekecewaan, kemarahan, solidaritas, dan harapan. Dengan demikian, penelitian ini menunjukkan bahwa Instagram berperan sebagai ruang diskursus publik digital yang penting dalam pembentukan opini, ekspresi emosi, dan evaluasi masyarakat terhadap komunikasi krisis pemerintah.

title: Agente conversacional para el Departamento de Inteligencia Artificial: evaluación del impacto de la verbalización de tablas y del tamaño de contexto en sistemas RAG
abstract: Este trabajo de fin de máster desarrolla y evalúa un agente conversacional basado en Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) para facilitar la consulta de guías docentes universitarias del Departamento de Inteligencia Artificial de la Universidad Politécnica de Madrid. El sistema permite formular preguntas en lenguaje natural sobre documentación académica y genera respuestas fundamentadas en fragmentos recuperados del corpus documental, reduciendo la necesidad de búsqueda manual en documentos PDF extensos y heterogéneos. El trabajo se centra en dos problemas relevantes para la aplicación de RAG sobre guías docentes. En primer lugar, se analiza el impacto de la verbalización de tablas, entendida como la transformación de información tabular en descripciones en lenguaje natural antes de la indexación. Esta técnica se evalúa comparando una configuración base, que mantiene las tablas en su representación original, con una configuración verbalizada. Los resultados muestran que la verbalización no produce una mejora uniforme en preguntas generales sobre el documento completo, ya que puede mejorar la recuperación de información relevante y la pertinencia de las respuestas, pero también introducir mayor redundancia y pérdida de precisión contextual. Sin embargo, en preguntas específicamente orientadas a información contenida en tablas, la verbalización sí aporta mejoras más consistentes, al facilitar la alineación semántica entre las consultas del usuario y los fragmentos indexados, manteniendo prácticamente estable la fidelidad de las respuestas. En segundo lugar, se estudia el tamaño óptimo del contexto recuperado (k), evaluando distintos valores de k, que determina el número de fragmentos incluidos en el prompt del modelo generativo. El análisis se realiza tanto con recuperación semántica directa como con una estrategia Multi-Query basada en reformulaciones de la consulta y fusión mediante Reciprocal Rank Fusion. Los resultados muestran que aumentar k mejora inicialmente la cobertura de información, pero a partir de valores intermedios introduce más ruido contextual, reduce la precisión media del contexto y aumenta la latencia de generación. En el dominio analizado, k=7 ofrece el mejor equilibrio entre cobertura, precisión, calidad de respuesta y coste computacional. La evaluación se realiza mediante RAGAS, utilizando métricas orientadas tanto a la recuperación como a la generación de respuestas. En conjunto, los resultados muestran que tanto la verbalización de tablas como la selección del tamaño de contexto son decisiones de diseño cuyo impacto depende del tipo de información que se desea recuperar. Mientras que la verbalización resulta especialmente útil para consultas sobre contenido tabular, el tamaño del contexto debe equilibrar la cobertura de información con la introducción de ruido documental. --ABSTRACT-- This Master’s Thesis develops and evaluates a conversational agent based on Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to facilitate access to university course guides from the Department of Artificial Intelligence at Universidad Politécnica de Madrid. The system allows users to ask natural language questions about academic documentation and generates answers grounded in fragments retrieved from the document corpus, reducing the need for manual search across long and heterogeneous PDF documents. The work focuses on two relevant challenges in the application of RAG to course guides. First, it analyzes the impact of table verbalization, understood as the transformation of tabular information into natural language descriptions before indexing. This technique is evaluated by comparing a baseline configuration, in which tables are kept in their original representation, with a verbalized configuration. The results show that verbalization does not lead to a uniform improvement for general questions about the whole document, since it can improve the retrieval of relevant information and the pertinence of the answers, but may also introduce greater redundancy and a loss of contextual precision. However, for questions specifically aimed at information contained in tables, verbalization provides more consistent improvements by facilitating the semantic alignment between user queries and indexed fragments, while keeping answer faithfulness practically stable. Second, the optimal size of the retrieved context (k) is studied by evaluating different values of k, which determines the number of fragments included in the prompt of the generative model. The analysis is carried out using both direct semantic retrieval and a Multi-Query strategy based on query reformulations and fusion through Reciprocal Rank Fusion. The results show that increasing k initially improves information coverage, but beyond intermediate values it introduces more contextual noise, reduces the average precision of the context and increases generation latency. In the analyzed domain, k=7 provides the best balance between coverage, precision, answer quality and computational cost. The evaluation is carried out using RAGAS, with metrics focused on both retrieval and answer generation. Overall, the results show that both table verbalization and the selection of context size are design decisions that depend on the type of query and the structure of the document corpus. Overall, the results show that both table verbalization and the selection of the retrieved context size are design decisions whose impact depends on the type of information being retrieved. While table verbalization is particularly beneficial for queries involving tabular content, the context size must balance information coverage against the introduction of documentary noise.

title: RAG enabled large language models
abstract: Η παρούσα πτυχιακή εργασία εξετάζει τη λειτουργία και τις δυνατότητες των Μεγάλων Γλωσσικών Μοντέλων (Large Language Models – LLMs) όταν συνδυάζονται με την αρχιτεκτονική Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), με σκοπό τη δημιουργία εξειδικευμένων συστημάτων παραγωγής λόγου υψηλής ποιότητας. Η αρχιτεκτονική RAG αποτελεί μια σύγχρονη προσέγγιση που ενισχύει τις δυνατότητες των μεγάλων γλωσσικών μοντέλων μέσω ανάκτησης σχετικής πληροφορίας από εξωτερικές βάσεις γνώσης, επιτρέποντας πιο ακριβή, τεκμηριωμένη και θεματικά στοχευμένη παραγωγή κειμένου. Στο πλαίσιο της εργασίας υλοποιήθηκε ένα σύστημα βασισμένο σε LLM και RAG, το οποίο εκπαιδεύτηκε πάνω σε λόγους παρουσιάσεων και keynote ανακοινώσεων μεγάλων τεχνολογικών εταιρειών σχετικά με πρωτοποριακά προϊόντα. Στόχος της υλοποίησης ήταν η δημιουργία ενός μοντέλου ικανού να παράγει κείμενα με ύφος παρουσίασης νέων προϊόντων. Η εργασία περιλαμβάνει τη θεωρητική ανάλυση των Μεγάλων Γλωσσικών Μοντέλων, την περιγραφή της αρχιτεκτονικής RAG, τη διαδικασία συλλογής και επεξεργασίας δεδομένων εκπαίδευσης, καθώς και την ανάπτυξη και αξιολόγηση του συστήματος.

title: Toward Real-Time Medical IVR in Latvian: Evaluation Framework and Comparative Analysis of STT and TTS Models
abstract: This article investigates state-of-the-art speech-to-text (STT) and text-to-speech (TTS) technologies for the development of a conversational interactive voice response (IVR) solution in the Latvian medical domain. The study addresses challenges associated with low-resource languages, domain-specific medical terminology, real-time interaction, and sensitive data processing. A requirement-driven evaluation framework is proposed that integrates linguistic and domain accuracy, architectural and deployment suitability, real-time performance, scalability, and regulatory considerations relevant to healthcare environments. Based on evidence reported in scientific literature, model documentation, and publicly available repositories, candidate STT and TTS models with Latvian support or adaptation potential are comparatively assessed against these requirements. Rather than providing a standardized experimental benchmark, the analysis identifies architectures and models whose documented characteristics appear most closely aligned with the operational requirements of real-time Latvian medical IVR deployment. The study provides a structured basis for candidate model selection and defines the metrics and deployment conditions to be addressed in subsequent common-condition empirical evaluation and clinical validation.

title: THE IMPLEMENTATION ROADMAP: FROM PILOT TO ENTERPRISE PRACTICAL STRATEGIES FOR OVERCOMING "PILOT PURGATORY," MEASURING AI ROI AND SCALING TECHNOLOGY ACROSS A LEGACY ORGANIZATION
abstract: Many organizations initiate Artificial Intelligence (AI) projects through small-scale pilots to explore the potential benefits of emerging technologies. However, a significant number of these initiatives fail to progress beyond the experimentation stage, resulting in what is commonly referred to as "pilot purgatory." This chapter presents a structured implementation roadmap that guides organizations from isolated AI pilots to enterprise-wide adoption. It discusses practical strategies for identifying high-value use cases, establishing governance frameworks, ensuring data readiness, and aligning AI initiatives with business objectives. The chapter also highlights methods for measuring AI return on investment (ROI) using operational, financial, and strategic performance indicators. Furthermore, it examines the challenges associated with integrating AI solutions into legacy systems and offers recommendations for change management, workforce readiness, and stakeholder engagement. By adopting a phased and scalable approach, organizations can minimize risks, maximize value creation, and achieve sustainable digital transformation through AI-driven innovation.

title: Agent-Based Contradiction Detection and Resolution for Multi-Source Retrieval Augmented Generation Systems
abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) attempts to mitigate the knowledge limitations of Large Language Models (LLMs) by letting them tap into outside sources.But in practice, things rarely run that smoothly.In realworld deployments, the assumption of uniform consistency across retrieved documents is often invalid.Pull from a mix of databases, and pretty quickly you end up with overlapping ideas and sources flat out contradicting each other.Passing conflicting evidence directly into an LLM typically results in hallucinations or factually incorrect responses.To resolve these inconsistencies systematically, we propose a modular, multi-agent system with LangGraph that puts some order into the chaos.Our architecture breaks the process into distinct steps, using eight agents to reshape raw text into clear factual statements, check for logical clashes, and weigh how trustworthy each source is, all based on the metadata.We score credibility by looking at things like how current the source is and its overall authority, then filter out the contradictions before the language model gets a final shot at generating answers.We put this framework to the test on a hand-picked set of 150 document pairs, all loaded with contradictions across legal, financial, and technical topics.The agent-based filtering boosted factual consistency up to 26.5% over Naive RAG compared to baseline RAG setups.Conclusion: integrating a dedicated contradictionchecking layer significantly improves the factual reliability of LLMs and a solid foundation for building applications people can trust.

title: When Will It Grok? Early, Cheap Prediction of Delayed Generalization, and How Far It Transfers
abstract: How early can grokking (delayed generalization) be predicted from cheap training signals, and does the predictor transfer across task families and optimizers? Grokking, though it appears as an abrupt late jump, is foreseeable early: from cheap scalar signals observed before memorization completes, a simple regressor predicts the grokking step with cross-validated R^2 up to 0.94, and 0.80 at just 50% training accuracy (45 grokked runs, 5 task families). The signal is the network's representational magnitude (logit scale/margin/weight norm, loo R^2 0.67-0.73) -- not gradient noise, and not the top Hessian eigenvalue (sharpness, 0.04). A robustness study shows the sharpness-negative is genuine (the estimate is converged to ~1%) and merely task-confounded (within-task sharper->sooner, cross-task sharper-tasks-later; Simpson reversal), not an artifact. The predictor RANK-transfers across task families (Spearman 0.84) but the ABSOLUTE timescale is idiosyncratic (R^2<0) -- a universal ordering, not a universal law. Whether grokking happens at all is DOUBLY gated: by the optimizer (AdamW 0.88; Adam/SGD ~0 despite a real search) and by the task (the quadratic family memorizes but never groks in budget). MECHANISM: the delay obeys the norm-separation law (replicated r=0.98; weight_norm is the tightest critical clock, CV 4.9%), and it holds at 8x scale (1.63M params). CONTROL: the mechanism is actionable -- switching weight decay at memorization steers the remaining delay as the law predicts (double->halve, r=0.996), and, driven by the paper's own early-signal predictor, it PROGRAMS heterogeneous tasks (natural-delay CV 0.51) to a common target grokking step -- within 6% with calibration (CV->0.05) or 16.5% end-to-end from the predictor alone. To our knowledge this is the first demonstration that delayed generalization can be steered to a chosen step. Net: grokking timing is early- and rank-predictable, idiosyncratic in scale, and steerable to a target; the right state variable is representational magnitude, not curvature.This manuscript was generated autonomously by the AI Scientist running inside Claude Code (Anthropic); every reported number traces to the project's experiment outputs. title: Cross-space Reconciliation SMOTE: Data Consistency Alignment and Generation Across Multiple Representation Spaces
abstract: Class imbalance is a pervasive challenge in machine learning, and the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) has been widely adopted to mitigate this issue by generating virtual minority samples. However, in the era of multi-modal and multi-view representation learning, data often co-exists across multiple heterogeneous representation spaces. Applying traditional SMOTE to each space independently disrupts the geometric alignment and cross-space mapping, leading to severe spatial distortion and "reconciliation failure" of the synthesized instances. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a novel framework named Cross-space Reconciliation SMOTE (CSR-SMOTE). The core of CSR-SMOTE lies in a global data consistency alignment mechanism. Instead of performing interpolation within an isolated feature space, CSR-SMOTE constructs a cross-space topological consensus matrix by fusing the local affinity behaviors from all representation spaces. We formulate the over-sampling process as a joint optimization problem, enforcing that the virtual samples across different spaces share an identical set of adaptive reconstruction coefficients. By alternatingly optimizing the virtual sample coordinates and the shared coefficients under topological constraints, the proposed algorithm ensures that the generated samples maintain strict entity-level alignment, geometric continuity, and manifold consistency across all representation spaces. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that CSR-SMOTE effectively preserves cross-view topology and exhibits strong robustness against local noise, offering a well-aligned and highly interpretable data augmentation solution for multi-view imbalanced learning.

title: RE-SMOTE: An Improved SMOTE Algorithm Based on Majority Class Redundancy Elimination
abstract: Class imbalance is a pervasive and challenging issue in machine learning and data mining. The traditional Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) alleviates this problem by interpolating between minority class samples, but it often ignores the internal distribution and redundancy of the majority class, leading to severe class overlapping and blurred decision boundaries. To address these limitations, this paper proposes an improved SMOTE algorithm based on redundancy elimination, termed RE-SMOTE. The core strategy of the proposed algorithm is to eliminate redundant majority class structures before generating compensation samples. In the first stage, the spatial local density and a boundary heterogeneity ratio are defined to identify and remove core redundant samples and invasive noise from the majority class, thereby clearing and optimizing the classification boundaries. In the second stage, an adaptive weight allocation mechanism is introduced to calculate the compensation requirements for each minority class sample based on the refined boundaries, and a modified linear interpolation method is used to precisely synthesize high-quality minority samples. This "reduction before compensation" strategy effectively maintains the intrinsic topological structure of the data and clarifies the decision boundaries. The theoretical framework demonstrates that RE-SMOTE significantly reduces data redundancy, mitigates over-fitting, and enhances the classification performance of classifiers on minority classes, providing a robust solution for imbalanced data mining.

title: W-SMOTE: An Oversampling Method Based on the Minimal Path of Wasserstein Distance for Imbalanced Learning
abstract: In the fields of machine learning and data mining, the class imbalance problem is ubiquitous across various real-world scenarios, such as credit fraud detection, medical diagnosis, and network intrusion detection. Traditional minority oversampling techniques, notably the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE), primarily generate synthetic samples via random linear interpolation within the Euclidean space. However, these methods often fail to account for the underlying geometric structures and probability distributions of the data, which inherently leads to blurry decision boundaries and overfitting. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a novel oversampling approach termed Wasserstein SMOTE (W-SMOTE). By incorporating the optimal transport theory, the proposed method utilizes the Wasserstein distance to measure the geodesic distances between the minority class samples and the global data distribution. Through generating synthetic samples along the Wasserstein barycenters and the minimal paths (displacement interpolations) in the space of probability measures, W-SMOTE can accurately capture the manifold structures of the minority class while preserving the statistical characteristics of the original distribution. Abandoning traditional empirical validations, this paper comprehensively establishes the mathematical framework of W-SMOTE, elucidates its optimization path from the perspectives of manifold learning and geometry, and theoretically demonstrates its superiority in mitigating boundary noise and maintaining topological integrity.

title: Propriedade intelectual e inteligência artificial: um debate e suas lacunas
abstract: A expansão da inteligência artificial tem tensionado os regimes jurídicos tradicionais de proteção à propriedade intelectual, especialmente no que se refere aos direitos autorais e à definição da autoria em contextos de automação criativa. Este artigo tem como objetivo analisar criticamente o descompasso entre regulação e inovação na proteção dos direitos autorais diante do desenvolvimento de sistemas de inteligência artificial no Brasil, à luz da tramitação do Projeto de Lei nº 2.338/2023. Adota-se uma abordagem exploratória e qualitativa, fundamentada em análise documental de projetos legislativos e em revisão bibliográfica da literatura nacional e internacional no campo da propriedade intelectual e dos estudos em Ciência, Tecnologia e Sociedade. Os resultados indicam que, embora o marco regulatório da inteligência artificial avance quanto à transparência, à remuneração dos titulares de direitos autorais e à incorporação de princípios éticos, persistem indefinições relevantes relacionadas à autoria de conteúdos gerados por IA, às obras derivadas, à proteção dos direitos morais e à responsabilidade civil por violações autorais. Conclui-se que tais lacunas evidenciam desafios sociotécnicos que demandam uma governança regulatória contínua, capaz de articular inovação tecnológica, proteção de direitos fundamentais e sustentabilidade cultural.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Causal Boosting: A Framework for Interpretable Attribution of Business Fluctuations
abstract: Attributing business fluctuations to actionable drivers is a critical component of decision-making in high-stakes domains. However, prevailing predictive models, predominantly driven by correlations, often yield inconsistent explanations that degrade under distribution shifts or latent confounding. Empirical causal inference to address this limitation remains challenge due to the identifiability gap in purely data-driven discovery and the complexity of encoding domain knowledge into differentiable learning pipelines. To bridge this gap, we propose Neuro-Symbolic Causal Boosting, a unified framework that integrates semantic domain priors with gradient-based causal estimation. First, we introduce the Complete Cause Identification Algorithm (CCIA). Unlike global search methods, CCIA recursively reconstructs the ancestral causal graph of the target variable by employing Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) as high-precision filters for low-order independence testing, coupled with a neuro-symbolic adjudication based on Large Language Model to resolve directionality. Subsequently, the identified structure scaffolds the Causal Additive Boosting Network (CABN). Grounded in the theory of structural identification, CABN enforces a reverse topological learning process. It utilizes weighted KANs to sequentially estimate downstream effects and adjust for confounding, thereby isolating invariant causal mechanisms. Empirical evaluation on a real-world telesales dataset and synthetic benchmarks demonstrates that our framework achieves a 57.5% reduction in Out-of-Distribution prediction error compared to strong correlation-based baselines. Additionally, it identifies and quantifies the impact of actionable drivers, providing a structured approach from observational data to trustworthy and interpretable business strategies.
